payload.description:
Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. ArmadaToken must be the Baal shares ERC20 with three enforced invariants: (1) a fixed 12,000,000e18 supply minted exactly once with no second mint path; (2) non-upgradeable code, with no proxy, no delegatecall in its runtime bytecode, and no _authorizeUpgrade-style path; (3) a transfer allowlist that only the timelock extends, that blocks every non-whitelisted transfer while transferable is false, that never blocks a mint (from==address(0)), and that lets the timelock alone call setTransferable(true) with no windDownContract dependency. Source: armada-laconic labbook 2026-10-18-treasury-governance-baal-safe-shielded §3 decisions 3,4,5 and §4 the G1 check; the committed brief armada-poc docs/tasks/G1-arm-shares-token.md.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. The source at armada-poc integrated meets these invariants, but no test proves them. A mutation that adds a second _mint call, converts the token to a proxy, or lets a non-whitelisted holder transfer, passes the current forge suite with no failure. The invariants are therefore unenforced.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run forge test. No test asserts, over its per-test pass/fail output: exactly one _mint call site in ArmadaToken.sol; the deployed runtime bytecode is immutable non-proxy code (no delegatecall); initWhitelist (deployer, one-shot) and addToWhitelist (timelock-only, add-only) gate as specified and a non-timelock caller reverts; a transfer from a non-whitelisted holder reverts with 'ArmadaToken: transfers restricted'; a mint (from==address(0)) is not blocked; setTransferable(true) succeeds from the timelock with windDownContract never set. A check reads forge test output and fails if any of these six assertions is absent, or passes under the mutation that breaks its invariant.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. The labbook decisions 3-5 describe code that armada-poc already has; if any property is not met, that is an escalation to the husband, not a silent contract edit. No windDownContract may be set in any test or deploy. Do not change circulatingSupplyOf, delegateOnBehalf/transferAndDelegate, or noDelegation. The existing forge suite must still pass unchanged. Follow the committed brief docs/tasks/G1-arm-shares-token.md for the deliverables.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) contracts/governance/ArmadaToken.sol

criticality: marginal

goal: Add forge tests that prove the six ArmadaToken invariants, plus a check that reads forge test output and confirms each assertion exists and catches its breaking mutation.

restatement:
  The ArmadaToken contract (contracts/governance/ArmadaToken.sol) must have its three design invariants enforced by the forge test suite, so a change that breaks one makes a test fail. The invariants: (1) a fixed supply of 12,000,000e18 is minted exactly once, with one _mint call site; (2) the code is non-upgradeable, with no proxy, no delegatecall in the runtime bytecode and no upgrade-authorization path; (3) the transfer allowlist is extended only by the timelock, blocks every non-whitelisted transfer while transferable is false, never blocks a mint, and lets the timelock alone call setTransferable(true) without any windDownContract. The contract already meets these now, so the work adds tests and does not edit the contract. A check reads the forge per-test results and fails if any of the six assertions is missing, or if it still passes when a mutation breaks its invariant. If the contract fails any invariant, the worker escalates and does not edit the contract.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: A forge test asserts that ArmadaToken.sol has exactly one _mint call site and that the fixed 12,000,000e18 supply is minted once.
- c2: A forge test asserts that the deployed runtime bytecode of ArmadaToken is immutable non-proxy code with no delegatecall.
- c3: A forge test asserts that initWhitelist (deployer, one-shot) and addToWhitelist (timelock-only, add-only) gate as specified, and that a non-timelock caller reverts.
- c4: A forge test asserts that a transfer from a non-whitelisted holder reverts with 'ArmadaToken: transfers restricted' while transferable is false.
- c5: A forge test asserts that a mint (from==address(0)) is not blocked by the transfer restriction.
- c6: A forge test asserts that setTransferable(true) succeeds from the timelock while windDownContract is never set.
- c7: A check reads forge test per-test pass/fail output and fails if any of the six assertions is absent, or if an assertion passes under the mutation that breaks its invariant (second _mint call, proxy conversion, non-whitelisted transfer allowed).
- c8: The existing forge suite still passes unchanged, no windDownContract is set in any test or deploy, and circulatingSupplyOf, delegateOnBehalf/transferAndDelegate and noDelegation are not changed.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: The checker reports that the single-mint test exists, passes on the real contract, and fails when a second _mint call is added.
- c2: The checker reports that the non-proxy bytecode test exists, passes on the real contract, and fails when the token is turned into a proxy.
- c3: The checker reports that the whitelist access tests exist, pass on the real contract, and fail when a non-timelock caller is allowed to extend the allowlist.
- c4: The checker reports that the restricted-transfer test exists, passes on the real contract, and fails when a non-whitelisted holder is allowed to transfer.
- c5: The checker reports that the mint-not-blocked test exists, passes on the real contract, and fails when the restriction also blocks minting.
- c6: The checker reports that the timelock-enables-transfers test exists, passes with windDownContract never set, and fails when setTransferable requires a windDownContract.
- c7: Run over all six assertions, the checker finds none missing and none that survive their breaking mutation.
- c8: The full existing forge suite passes, no test or deploy sets windDownContract, and the protected delegation and supply functions are unchanged.

Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. A summon script must deploy one Baal (Moloch v3; HausDAO feat/baalZodiac, the version the labbook records audited by Hacken 2022-08-02 and Quantstamp 2022-10-18) backed by one Gnosis Safe, with ARM (ArmadaToken) as the Baal shares token, the Safe's only owner set to the Baal contract, and the Safe's threshold set to 1. The deploy joins the fixturenet setup chain after ARM deploys. Source: armada-laconic labbook 2026-10-18-treasury-governance-baal-safe-shielded 3 decisions 1,8,9,10 and 4 the G2 check; the committed brief armada-poc docs/tasks/G2-baal-safe-summon.md.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. The repo has no Safe or Baal contracts (lib/ holds only forge-std and halmos-cheatcodes; no .gitmodules), no summon script, and no governance-baal deploy step in package.json scripts.setup. The Baal treasury governance design is unimplemented.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. A fixturenet deploy (npm run setup, or the new governance-baal step alone) must print: the Safe address with zero human owners and threshold 1; the Baal address with ARM as its registered shares token; safe.isOwner(baal)==true and safe.getOwners().length==1. A forge test on a local EVM must assert the same three facts. A check reads those printed fields and the test pass/fail output and fails if a human Safe owner exists at any point, if ARM is not Baal's shares token, or if the Safe is not owned solely by Baal at threshold 1.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Vendor Safe (safe-contracts) and Baal (feat/baalZodiac) at the audited commits the labbook names; confirm the commit hashes from the feat/baalZodiac branch tip. No human Safe owner at any point in the deploy, even transiently. Depends on G1 (ArmadaToken as the Baal shares token). payload.description:
original_statement:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. ArmadaCrowdfund.finalize must create one Safe-owned shielded note for the sale proceeds in the same call, instead of sending the proceeds USDC to the treasury address. Source: armada-laconic labbook 2026-10-18-treasury-governance-baal-safe-shielded 3 decision 16 and 4 the G5 check; P2-CONTRACT item 6; the committed brief armada-poc docs/tasks/G5-hedgey-crowdfund-shielded-proceeds.md S1.
  What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. ArmadaCrowdfund.finalize pays proceedsPush with usdc.safeTransfer(treasury, proceedsPush), so the proceeds rest at the treasury public address. No test proves the proceeds become a Safe-owned note.
  How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run forge test --match-path test-foundry/CrowdfundShieldedProceeds.t.sol. After finalize, the pool holds a Safe-owned note for proceedsPush, read via preimageOf, and the treasury address USDC balance is unchanged by finalize. A check fails if the proceeds sit at the treasury public address after finalize.
  What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Depends on G1 (merged) and P2b (merged; the pool shield path, the Safe owner-derived npk, and preimageOf). Change only the proceeds transfer to a shield to the Safe's npk; keep the treasury immutable and finalize nonReentrant. Copy the shield pattern from contracts/privacy-pool/modules/ShieldModule.sol and the setup from test-foundry/CrowdfundFullInvariant.t.sol. A sibling piece adds the allowance, reentrancy and unsold-ARM-sweep hardening tests.
  Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) contracts/crowdfund/ArmadaCrowdfund.sol finalize

criticality: critical

goal: ArmadaCrowdfund.finalize shields the sale proceeds into one Safe-owned note in the same call, instead of sending the proceeds USDC to the treasury address.

restatement:
  When ArmadaCrowdfund.finalize runs, the sale proceeds (proceedsPush) must not be sent as USDC to the public treasury address with usdc.safeTransfer(treasury, proceedsPush). In the same call, finalize must shield exactly proceedsPush into the privacy pool as one note owned by the Safe, using the Safe's owner-derived npk. The pool must hold that note, readable through preimageOf. The treasury address USDC balance must be unchanged by finalize. Only the proceeds transfer changes. The treasury stays immutable and finalize stays nonReentrant. The change is observed with forge test --match-path test-foundry/CrowdfundShieldedProceeds.t.sol, and a check fails if the proceeds sit at the treasury public address after finalize.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: After finalize, the pool holds one Safe-owned note for proceedsPush, created in the same finalize call and read via preimageOf, using the Safe's npk.
- c2: The treasury address USDC balance is unchanged by finalize, so the proceeds do not sit at the treasury public address after finalize.
- c3: finalize stays nonReentrant: a reentrant call made during finalize is rejected.
- c4: The treasury address stays immutable: the treasury value is the same before and after finalize.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: After the crowdfund is finalized, the pool holds a note owned by the Safe for exactly the sale proceeds amount, and reading it back through preimageOf shows the Safe's owner key and that amount.
- c2: The treasury address holds the same USDC amount before and after the crowdfund is finalized, so no proceeds are left at the public treasury address.
- c3: A call back into finalize while finalize is running is refused, and the finalize call keeps its protection against re-entry.
- c4: The treasury address reported by the crowdfund is identical before and after finalize.

criticality: marginal

goal: RevenueLock bounds each release on pool.cumulativeFees(asset) for one named asset and no longer uses RevenueCounter.recognizedRevenueUsd or a daily-increase ratchet.

restatement:
  RevenueLock must base each release on the fees the pool has really collected. It must read pool.cumulativeFees(asset) for one named asset, inside the call. It must not read RevenueCounter.recognizedRevenueUsd, which the owner raises for free. It must not apply any daily-increase ratchet. The constructor takes pool and asset in place of the RevenueCounter. The old source code is deleted: maxObservedRevenue, MAX_REVENUE_INCREASE_PER_DAY, the sync path, and getCappedObservedRevenue. The milestone step function and its constants stay unchanged. A caller that pays no fees must not be able to raise the release source. The releasable view and release must give the same number, bit for bit. Tests run by forge test --match-path test-foundry/RevenueLock.t.sol must prove this. The wind-down freeze, RevenueCounter.sol and RevenueReserveDistributor.sol are out of scope and must not change.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: RevenueLock must bound each release on pool.cumulativeFees(asset) for one named asset, read inside the call.
- c2: RevenueLock must not read RevenueCounter.recognizedRevenueUsd.
- c3: RevenueLock must not apply any daily-increase ratchet: maxObservedRevenue, MAX_REVENUE_INCREASE_PER_DAY, the sync path, and getCappedObservedRevenue are deleted.
- c4: The RevenueCounter source and its constructor dependency are replaced with pool and asset.
- c5: No function may let a non-fee-paying caller raise the release source; the release entitlement tracks pool.cumulativeFees(asset).
- c6: releasable and release must agree bit-for-bit.
- c7: The milestone step function and its constants stay unchanged.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: When the pool's recorded fees for the named asset go up, the amount that can be released moves with them and is capped by those fees.
- c2: The owner raises the revenue figure in the old revenue counter, and the amount that can be released does not change.
- c3: The pool's fees jump past a milestone in a single day, and the full milestone amount can be released at once, with no daily limit.
- c4: The lock is built with a pool address and an asset, and it releases against that pool and that asset only. Fees on another asset have no effect.
- c5: An account that pays no fees tries every public action, and the amount that can be released does not rise.
- c6: At many fee levels and times, the releasable figure equals the amount that release actually pays out.
- c7: The release steps at the same milestone points as before, with the same constants, when fees cross each milestone.

A Baal manager shaman named ShieldedRagequit must let any caller burn armAmount of their own ARM and receive, as a contract-owned note to their own npk, exactly burned/totalSupply times the Safe's balance of each listed token, with no treasury signature and no quorum, and never more than that bound. It is the only shaman Baal registers. Source: armada-laconic labbook 2026-10-18-treasury-governance-baal-safe-shielded 3 decisions 12,13,14,15,16,20,21 and 4 the G3 check; P2-CONTRACT items 1,2,3 and 6; the committed brief armada-poc docs/tasks/G3-shielded-ragequit.md.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. No ShieldedRagequit contract exists. ArmadaToken has no burn. There is no path for a holder to exit the treasury for a pro-rata contract-owned note, and no test proves the exit is unblockable by a captured majority or bounded against over-payment.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run forge test --match-path test-foundry/ShieldedRagequit.t.sol. ragequit must burn the caller's ARM and reduce totalSupply; create a contract-owned note at the caller's npk with the bounded payout, read via preimageOf; succeed with no Safe signature and no Baal proposal; revert a crafted call that claims more than the bound; and leave Baal's shaman list holding exactly ShieldedRagequit. A check reads the test pass/fail output and fails if the exit pays more than burned/totalSupply times treasury, if it needs the treasury's signature or a proposal, or if the shaman list is not exactly ShieldedRagequit. Plus, using armada-sdk, a built exit proof for the resulting note must verify on-chain through PrivacyPool.transact.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Depends on G2 (Baal and Safe summon, merged) and P2b (merged; transactOwned, preimageOf, the owner-derived npk binding the spent note to the Safe). Add a burn to ArmadaToken callable only by ShieldedRagequit, mirroring the one-shot authorized-caller pattern. Compute the payout bound from balances read inside the same transaction, holding for every call ordering including two ragequits in one block. SafeERC20 for every token call; emit an event for every holdings change. Follow the committed brief docs/tasks/G3-shielded-ragequit.md deliverables in full.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) contracts/governance/ShieldedRagequit.sol, contracts/governance/ArmadaToken.sol (burn), contracts/privacy-pool/PrivacyPool.sol (transactOwned)

criticality: critical

goal: Any ARM holder can burn their ARM through ShieldedRagequit and receive, as a contract-owned note at their own npk, exactly burned/totalSupply times the Safe's balance of each listed token, with no treasury signature, no quorum, and never more than that bound; the note is spendable on-chain.

restatement:
  Armada needs a treasury exit that a holder can use alone, at any time, and that a captured governance majority cannot block. A new Baal manager shaman, ShieldedRagequit (contracts/governance/ShieldedRagequit.sol), takes the ARM token, the Baal address, the Safe address and the PrivacyPool address in its constructor. Its function ragequit(uint256 armAmount, bytes32 npk, address[] tokens) burns armAmount of the caller's own ARM. For each listed token it pays exactly armAmount * safe.balanceOf(token) / armToken.totalSupply(), read inside the same transaction. The payout is a contract-owned note CommitmentPreimage{npk, token, payout} at the caller's own npk. The pool's transactOwned creates the note by spending a Safe-owned pool note and returning a Safe-owned change note. The exit needs no treasury signature and no Baal proposal. It never pays more than the bound, for every call order, including two ragequits in one block. ArmadaToken gains a burn that only ShieldedRagequit can call, set once through the one-shot authorized-caller pattern (as addAuthorizedDelegator). ShieldedRagequit is the only shaman that Baal registers. Every token call uses SafeERC20. Every holdings change emits RagequitExecuted. The payout note is a real spendable note: an exit proof that armada-sdk builds with planSpend and prove for that note verifies on-chain through PrivacyPool.transact. The acceptance is forge test --match-path test-foundry/ShieldedRagequit.t.sol plus that SDK exit-proof check.

restatement_clauses:
- C1: ragequit must burn the caller's armAmount of ARM and reduce totalSupply by armAmount.
- C2: ragequit must create a contract-owned note at the caller's npk with payout = armAmount * safe.balanceOf(token) / armToken.totalSupply(), read via preimageOf on the resulting commitment, debited from a Safe-owned pool note with a Safe-owned change note.
- C3: ragequit must succeed with no Safe signature and no Baal proposal; a test where the exit needs the treasury's signature or a proposal must fail.
- C4: A crafted call that claims more than armAmount * safe.balanceOf(token) / armToken.totalSupply() must revert, and the burn leaves no path to credit ARM back on a reverted or partial payout.
- C5: The payout bound must hold for every call ordering, including two ragequits in one block against the same token, computed from balances read inside the same transaction.
- C6: Baal's shaman list must hold exactly ShieldedRagequit and no other shaman.
- C7: ArmadaToken must have a burn callable only by ShieldedRagequit, set through a one-shot authorized-caller pattern mirroring addAuthorizedDelegator; any other caller must revert.
- C8: ragequit must not create a note for a token the Safe does not hold as a pool-owned note.
- C9: Every holdings change must emit RagequitExecuted(address indexed holder, uint256 armBurned, bytes32 npk, address[] tokens, uint256[] payouts), and every token call must use SafeERC20.
- C10: Using armada-sdk, an exit proof built with planSpend and prove for the ragequit payout note must verify on-chain through PrivacyPool.transact.

acceptance_criteria:
- C1: After a holder exits, their ARM balance and the total ARM supply both fall by exactly the amount they gave up, and the check also catches every small deliberate fault put into the new contract code.
- C2: After an exit, reading the new note back from the pool shows the holder's own key, the right token, and a value equal to their share of the treasury balance; the treasury keeps a change note for the rest.
- C3: A holder completes an exit with no treasury signer and no governance proposal involved, and the exit still succeeds.
- C4: An attempt to take more than the holder's share is refused, and after the refusal the holder's ARM balance and the treasury are unchanged.
- C5: Two holders exit in the same block against the same token, in both orders; each receives exactly their share of the balance at the time of their exit, and the total paid never exceeds the treasury's holding.
- C6: After the treasury setup and the exit contract registration, Baal's list of special-permission modules has exactly one entry, and that entry is the exit contract.
- C7: Any account other than the exit contract that tries to burn ARM is refused, and a second attempt to set the authorized burner is refused.
- C8: An exit that lists a token the treasury does not hold in the pool is refused, and no note is created for it.
- C9: Each exit announces the holder, the ARM burned, the holder's key, the tokens and the amounts paid; an exit that lists a token with no standard return value still completes correctly.
- C10: The holder builds a spend proof for their exit note with the Armada wallet library, and the pool accepts it on a real local chain; the value spent equals the value of the outputs, and the pool refuses the same proof when its amount is changed.

Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. A Baal manager shaman named ShieldedRagequit must let any caller burn armAmount of their own ARM and receive, as a contract-owned note to their own npk, exactly burned/totalSupply times the Safe's balance of each listed token, with no treasury signature and no quorum, and never more than that bound. It is the only shaman Baal registers. Source: armada-laconic labbook 2026-10-18-treasury-governance-baal-safe-shielded 3 decisions 12,13,14,15,16,20,21 and 4 the G3 check; P2-CONTRACT items 1,2,3 and 6; the committed brief armada-poc docs/tasks/G3-shielded-ragequit.md.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. No ShieldedRagequit contract exists. ArmadaToken has no burn. There is no path for a holder to exit the treasury for a pro-rata contract-owned note, and no test proves the exit is unblockable by a captured majority or bounded against over-payment.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run forge test --match-path test-foundry/ShieldedRagequit.t.sol. ragequit must burn the caller's ARM and reduce totalSupply; create a contract-owned note at the caller's npk with the bounded payout, read via preimageOf; succeed with no Safe signature and no Baal proposal; revert a crafted call that claims more than the bound; revert a call from a caller that holds no ARM, creating no note and leaving the Safe balances and ARM totalSupply unchanged; and leave Baal's shaman list holding exactly ShieldedRagequit. A check reads the test pass/fail output and fails if the exit pays more than burned/totalSupply times treasury, if it needs the treasury's signature or a proposal, if a non-holder caller receives any note, or if the shaman list is not exactly ShieldedRagequit. Plus, using armada-sdk, a built exit proof for the resulting note must verify on-chain through PrivacyPool.transact.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Depends on G2 (Baal and Safe summon, merged) and P2b (merged; transactOwned, preimageOf, the owner-derived npk binding the spent note to the Safe). Add a burn to ArmadaToken callable only by ShieldedRagequit, mirroring the one-shot authorized-caller pattern. Compute the payout bound from balances read inside the same transaction, holding for every call ordering including two ragequits in one block. SafeERC20 for every token call; emit an event for every holdings change. Follow the committed brief docs/tasks/G3-shielded-ragequit.md deliverables in full.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) contracts/governance/ShieldedRagequit.sol, contracts/governance/ArmadaToken.sol (burn), contracts/privacy-pool/PrivacyPool.sol (transactOwned)

criticality: critical

goal: Any ARM holder can exit the Baal/Safe treasury alone for an exact, bounded pro-rata share. The share arrives as a spendable shielded note, and no majority can block the exit.

restatement:
  Armada needs a treasury exit that a captured majority cannot block and that cannot over-pay. A new Baal manager shaman, ShieldedRagequit (contracts/governance/ShieldedRagequit.sol), lets any ARM holder call ragequit(armAmount, npk, tokens). The call burns armAmount of the caller's own ARM through a new ArmadaToken burn function. Only ShieldedRagequit can call that burn function, which follows the one-shot authorized-caller pattern of addAuthorizedDelegator. For each listed token, the call pays exactly armAmount * safe.balanceOf(token) / armToken.totalSupply(), never more. The contract reads these balances inside the same transaction. It pays through PrivacyPool.transactOwned as a contract-owned note at the caller's npk, debited from a Safe-owned pool note. The call needs no Safe signature and no Baal proposal. A caller with no ARM gets a revert, no note, and no change to Safe balances or ARM totalSupply. The bound holds for every call order, including two ragequits in one block. Every holdings change emits RagequitExecuted. Every token call uses SafeERC20. ShieldedRagequit is the only shaman that Baal registers. An armada-sdk exit proof (planSpend + prove) for the resulting payout note verifies on-chain through PrivacyPool.transact. This proves that the payout is a real, spendable note. The work follows docs/tasks/G3-shielded-ragequit.md in full.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: ragequit burns armAmount of the caller's ARM and reduces ARM totalSupply by armAmount.
- c2: ragequit creates a contract-owned note at the caller's npk with payout exactly armAmount * safe.balanceOf(token) / armToken.totalSupply() for each listed token, confirmed by reading preimageOf on the resulting commitment.
- c3: ragequit succeeds with no Safe signature and no Baal proposal; an exit that needs the treasury's signature or a proposal fails the check.
- c4: A crafted call that claims more than burned/totalSupply times the Safe's balance of a token reverts.
- c5: A ragequit call from a caller that holds no ARM reverts, creates no note, and leaves the Safe balances and ARM totalSupply unchanged.
- c6: Baal's shaman list holds exactly one entry, ShieldedRagequit.
- c7: ArmadaToken's burn is callable only by ShieldedRagequit; any other caller reverts.
- c8: The payout bound holds for every call ordering, including two ragequits in the same block against the same token: the total paid never exceeds each holder's burned/totalSupply share of the Safe balance read in that holder's transaction.
- c9: Every ragequit holdings change emits RagequitExecuted(holder, armBurned, npk, tokens, payouts) with the actual values.
- c10: Using armada-sdk planSpend and prove, an exit proof built for the ragequit payout note verifies on-chain through PrivacyPool.transact, and the spend conserves value: the spent payout value equals the sum of the spend outputs.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: After a holder exits, the holder's ARM balance and the total ARM supply both fall by exactly the amount the holder gave up.
- c2: After an exit, the pool records a new note for the holder's own key, and its amount equals the holder's exact share of the treasury.
- c3: A holder exits with one direct call, and no treasury signer and no governance vote takes part.
- c4: An attempt to take more than the holder's fair share is refused, and the treasury keeps its funds.
- c5: A caller with no ARM who tries to exit is refused, gets no note, and the treasury balances and total ARM supply stay the same.
- c6: After setup, the governance contract lists exactly one special-power module, and it is the exit module.
- c7: Any account other than the exit module that tries to destroy ARM is refused.
- c8: Two holders exit one after the other in the same block. Each holder gets no more than a fair share of the balance present at that holder's exit. The treasury never pays out more than it held.
- c9: Each exit publishes a public record. The record names the holder, the amount burned, the destination key, the tokens, and the amounts paid.
- c10: The holder's wallet builds a spend for the payout note that the exit created. The pool accepts that spend on-chain. The value that the spend consumes equals the value that it creates.

What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. The owner is a single key or a Safe multisig, never a DAO-governed contract. VerifierModule.setVerificationKey stays owner-callable by design (issue #349); this concerns who holds that authority, not removing it. The pool is already not a proxy; this is verification, not a redesign.

Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. The armada-poc repository contains no governor, treasury-governor, steward, wind-down, or redemption contract. Baal (G2) and the Safe are the only on-chain governance surface. GOVERNANCE.md and ARM_TOKEN.md describe only the contracts that remain: Baal and the Safe, ShieldedRagequit (G3), RevenueLock on cumulativeFees (G4), the Hedgey lockup (G5), and ArmadaToken as the fixed-supply Baal shares token (G1).
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. The repository still carries ArmadaGovernor.sol, ArmadaTreasuryGov.sol, TreasurySteward.sol, ArmadaWindDown.sol, ArmadaRedemption.sol, contracts/periphery/RedemptionRouter.sol, and MockRedemptionDeps.sol. It still carries the governor, steward, and wind-down test files. The IArmadaGovernance.sol interface still declares IArmadaGovernorTiming and ITreasurySteward. package.json still runs the old governor, treasury-gov, steward, wind-down, and redemption deploy steps. A grep for the five deleted names across contracts/ and scripts/ lists 28 files. GOVERNANCE.md and ARM_TOKEN.md do not exist.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run grep -rlE 'ArmadaGovernor|ArmadaTreasuryGov|TreasurySteward|ArmadaWindDown|ArmadaRedemption' contracts/ scripts/. Today it lists 28 files; after the change it lists none. Run forge build: it succeeds with no reference to a deleted contract. Run forge test: no import fails. A check reads the grep match count, the forge build exit code, and the forge test result. The check fails if any deleted name survives in contracts/ or scripts/, if the build fails, or if a test import fails. The GOVERNANCE.md and ARM_TOKEN.md files exist and describe only the remaining design.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Depends on G2 (Baal and Safe summon) and G5 (crowdfund shielded proceeds and Hedgey lockup), both merged. Keep IAdapterRegistry in IArmadaGovernance.sol: ShieldModule.sol uses it. Keep RevenueCounter.sol and RevenueReserveDistributor.sol unless the grep shows no surviving caller. Delete a file with a surviving caller only after you update that caller in the same change. Remove the old governor, treasury-gov, steward, wind-down, and redemption deploy steps from package.json's setup chain; the G2 Baal and Safe summon script takes their place. Follow docs/tasks/G6-remove-old-stack-docs.md steps S1 through S5.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) contracts/governance/, contracts/periphery/RedemptionRouter.sol, test-foundry/, test/, package.json, GOVERNANCE.md, ARM_TOKEN.md

Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. The Hub PrivacyPool must be non-upgradeable, and the authority that can set its verification keys — the pool owner — must not be an address the governance DAO can reach. A swapped verification key would let an attacker accept forged proofs and drain every pool user's shielded funds.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. No test proves the pool exposes no upgrade entry point, no test proves the owner is not a governance-controlled address, and no test proves only the owner can set a verification key. The hub deploy path sets the owner to the deployer and never checks it against the governance deployment's own contract addresses, and offers no dedicated owner-key input.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. The tests prove behaviour these existing contract files already have. The no-upgrade-entry-point and owner-is-not-governance tests exercise contracts/privacy-pool/PrivacyPool.sol (it has no upgradeTo(address) or upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes) entry point, and sets owner once in initialize). The owner-only-setVerificationKey test exercises the owner gate in contracts/privacy-pool/PrivacyPool.sol and contracts/privacy-pool/modules/VerifierModule.sol. To see the deploy gap, read scripts/deploy_privacy_pool.ts deployHub: it passes deployer.address as the pool owner and never compares it to the governance deployment's governor, treasury or wind-down addresses, and has no POOL_OWNER_ADDRESS override.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. The owner is a single key or a Safe multisig, never a DAO-governed contract. VerifierModule.setVerificationKey stays owner-callable by design (issue #349); this concerns who holds that authority, not removing it. The pool is already not a proxy; this is verification plus a deploy-script guard, not a contract redesign.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) armada-poc Hub PrivacyPool contracts (contracts/privacy-pool/PrivacyPool.sol, modules/VerifierModule.sol) and the hub deploy (scripts/deploy_privacy_pool.ts)

criticality: critical

goal: Baal counts each holder's ARM (ArmadaToken) balance as that holder's vote power, with one ARM token and a timestamp clock that matches Baal's vote lookup.

restatement:
  Armada governance must have exactly one vote token, and that token is ArmadaToken (ARM). The ARM a holder receives from the crowdfund, and the ARM that ShieldedRagequit burns, must be the same ARM that Baal counts as vote power. So the Baal summon flow in scripts/summon-baal-safe.ts must register the ArmadaToken address as Baal's shares token. The separate contract contracts/governance/BaalSharesToken.sol must stop being the shares token, because nothing mints it and every holder reads 0 votes. Baal.submitVote reads getPastVotes at prop.votingStarts, which is a block timestamp. So ArmadaToken must use a timestamp clock: CLOCK_MODE() must contain the word timestamp, and getPastVotes(holder, a past timestamp) must equal the holder's delegated ARM balance at that timestamp. A crowdfund claim must raise the claimant's ARM balance and past votes by the allocation. A ragequit must lower the holder's ARM balance and the ARM total supply by the burned amount. ARM stays a plain non-upgradeable ERC20 with 12,000,000e18 minted once and no later mint path. Only the ragequit shaman can burn. The transfer allowlist is fixed at construction. The vendored Baal in lib/baal (feat/baalZodiac) stays unchanged.

The only burn path is ArmadaToken.burn(account, amount), callable only by the ShieldedRagequit shaman. ShieldedRagequit stays the one exit that burns ARM and pays a note. GOVERNANCE.md states the Safe is the treasury with the Baal as its sole owner, and ShieldedRagequit is the one exit.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. G6 (arp-93a) deleted scripts/deploy_governance.ts, which wrote getGovernanceDeploymentFile. Nothing writes it now. Six scripts read its fields and throw 'Governance deployment not found': deploy_privacy_pool.ts reads treasury; deploy_fee_module.ts reads treasury, timelockController, governor and revenueCounter; deploy_crowdfund.ts reads armToken, treasury, revenueLock and revenueReserveDistributor; deploy_yield.ts reads adapterRegistry and treasury; deploy_revenue_lock_cohort.ts reads armToken and revenueCounter; link_privacy_pool.ts reads timelockController, adapterRegistry and shieldPauseController. No script calls setShamans and ShieldedRagequit has no deploy script. summon-baal-safe.ts reads armToken from the missing manifest and deploys its own Safe.

payload.body: Superseded by arp-e44. The deploy-suite migration merged on integrated at d4ddbbe2 (bus close 1f07f220). deploy_governance.ts writes the full Baal-era manifest; summon-baal-safe.ts deploys ShieldedRagequit before Baal.setUp and registers it as the one manager shaman through the setUp init multisend; deploy_crowdfund.ts and deploy_revenue_lock_cohort.ts use the current contract constructors. All seven acceptance clauses in scripts/check-governance-deploy.sh pass on a local anvil.

Forbidden-owner set under the Baal/Safe stack (replaces the old governor/treasury/wind-down set, which G6 removed and arp-67a's manifest does not reproduce). The pool owner must not equal any address the Baal/Safe governance can direct: (1) the Baal contract; (2) the Baal avatar Safe, which is the treasury; (3) the ShieldedRagequit shaman; (4) the ARM token. The deploy reads these from the committed manifests. The governance manifest (getGovernanceDeploymentFile) records contracts.treasury = the Safe and contracts.armToken. The Baal/Safe manifest (getBaalSafeDeploymentFile) records contracts.baal, contracts.safe and contracts.shieldedRagequit. The pool treasury is the Safe; deploy_privacy_pool.ts resolves it from govDeployment.contracts.treasury, which exists again after arp-67a (commit d4ddbbe2). There is no governor, no timelock and no wind-down contract; the manifest governor field equals the Safe. The deploy guard must throw before the initialize transaction if the resolved owner equals any forbidden address, and must name the address that collided. summon-baal-safe.ts registers ShieldedRagequit as the one shaman, so the guard is gradeable on a local hub chain.

goal: After the one-shot burner registration, the set of ArmadaToken burners is frozen to ShieldedRagequit. No address, the timelock/Safe included, can add a burner.

restatement:

The intent is that this set is fixed at deploy: the deployer registers ShieldedRagequit one time through the one-shot initBurners, and after that registration no address can extend the set. Today addBurner lets the immutable timelock address (the Safe, per scripts/deploy_governance.ts) authorize any number of further burners, and each new burner could destroy ARM from any wallet. The fix removes that post-deploy path in contracts/governance/ArmadaToken.sol. It also updates every deploy script, task, or test that calls addBurner. After the change, a call from the timelock that tries to authorize a new burner fails, and authorizedBurner for that address stays false. The deployer and every other address also cannot add a burner after the one-shot registration, and a second initBurners call fails. ShieldedRagequit still burns ARM successfully. Any other caller of burn reverts with "ArmadaToken: not authorized burner". A forge test proves these outcomes.

- C1: After deploy, the timelock (the Safe) tries to give burn rights to a new address. The attempt fails, and the new address still has no burn rights.

- C3: ShieldedRagequit burns an amount of ARM from a holder. The call succeeds, and the holder's ARM balance and the total supply both drop by that amount.
- C4: An address that is not ShieldedRagequit (the timelock, the deployer, or a random address) tries to burn a holder's ARM. Each call fails with the message "ArmadaToken: not authorized burner", and the holder's balance does not change.
- C5: The existing shielded-ragequit tests in test-foundry/ShieldedRagequit.t.sol set up the token with the one-time registration only, and a member ragequit still burns that member's ARM.
